name: Maroon Pigeon
rangeDescription: Forest of são tomé (gulf of guinea)
description: A large, very dark pigeon with a grayish head, a burgundy body with scattered small white spots, and a bright yellow bill and legs. Female is duller than the male.

name: Short-tailed Parrot
rangeDescription: Southeastern colombia to eastern ecuador, eastern peru, and brazil north of the amazon
description: Medium-sized, uniformly bright green parrot with a short tail. Note the indistinct black eye-line, the dusky bill, and the darker green flight feathers; other parrots have more colorful plumage and longer tails.

name: Ground Woodpecker
rangeDescription: South africa and lesotho
description: A large, sociable, ground-loving woodpecker of open, lightly-vegetated country, where it prefers to perch on rocks. It has grayish olive upperparts, pale eyes, and a pink washed breast.

name: Watercock
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southern and eastern asia and malay archipelago
description: Large, distinctive marsh dweller, elusive and often difficult to see in the heavily vegetated wet fields and marshes it inhabits. Male is unmistakable, with black body, brown-edged wing coverts, and red-and-yellow bill with raised, spiky red frontal shield (unlike smaller moorhen).

name: Black-headed Hemispingus
rangeDescription: Andes of colombia to southwestern venezuela and far northern peru
description: A unique little songbird found in the temperate zone of the Andes from extreme western Venezuela to northern Peru. Not bright, but distinctively patterned with a black head, a buffy central crown stripe, staring pale eyes, and a gray body.

name: White-necked Parakeet
rangeDescription: Humid lowlands of southeastern ecuador
description: Colorful, long-tailed parakeet restricted to Andean cloud forest in southeastern Ecuador and extreme northern Peru near the border. Combination of white neck, buffy breast, and orange cheek patch separates it from all other parakeets.

name: Malayan Whistling-Thrush
rangeDescription: Moist montane forest of central malaya
description: Dark bluish thrush-like bird with a bright yellow bill. Found solely in the highlands of peninsular Malaysia.

name: Gray-headed Robin
rangeDescription: Rainforest of northern queensland (cooktown to mount spec)
description: Large, plump robin of montane rainforest. Both sexes olive brown above, with gray crown and breast, stark white throat, and white wing patch, prominent in flight.

name: White-naped Jay
rangeDescription: Tableland of eastern brazil (pará to minas gerais and eastern mato grosso)
description: Large jay with piercing yellow eyes and stiff forehead feathers. Note the blue patches above and below the eyes, contrasting with the black face.

name: Bocage's Weaver
rangeDescription: Riparian grassland of angola to southeastern democratic republic of the congo and northwestern zambia
description: A fairly large weaver with a long thin pointed bill. The male has a pale eye, and during the breeding season a brownish wash to the ear.

name: Black-crowned Pitta
rangeDescription: Lowlands of northern borneo
description: Dazzling pitta of Borneo’s lowland dipterocarp forests. Midnight blue above and blinding scarlet below, with a dark head, bright blue wing coverts, and a glowing silver line trailing backwards behind the eye.

name: Bahia Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Montane forest of southeastern brazil (southern bahia near boa nova)
description: Small flycatcher with a long tail that is usually held cocked. Has an olive-green back, a whitish throat, and yellowish underparts.

name: Santa Cruz Ground Dove
rangeDescription: Tinakula and utupua (northern and central temotu, southeastern solomon islands), and vanuatu
description: A rotund, short-legged ground-dwelling dove that usually runs rather than flies when startled. Male has a dark body with an iridescent pinkish-purple shoulder patch, a cream-colored chest, and a gray head.

name: Painted Tody-Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Southern venezuela to the guianas and northern brazil (east of rio negro)
description: Tiny bird of forest canopy; difficult to see well and heard far more than seen. Appears mostly yellow from below.

name: Crescent-faced Antpitta
rangeDescription: Locally in andes of southern colombia and ecuador
description: Small, striking antpitta that lurks in bamboo-laden cloud forest at very high elevations in the Andes. Brown and gray with white crescents on face, streaked underparts, and buffy spots on sides of neck.

name: Black-backed Water-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Amazonian and eastern brazil to eastern bolivia, paraguay, and northern argentina
description: Medium-sized flycatcher, usually seen walking on the ground around marshy areas, lakes, and rivers. Mostly white below and on the face contrasting with a black crown and back, a white rump and two white wingbars.

name: Chattering Cisticola
rangeDescription: Nigeria to cameroon, gabon, congo, democratic republic of the congo, and northwestern angola
description: A common, nondescript bird found near the ground in grassy areas in fields, in towns, along roads, and even in larger treefall gaps in lowland rainforest. Small and warbler-like, with a white throat, dingy white underparts, a brownish red cap, and brownish upperparts.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Jamaican Mango
rangeDescription: Jamaica
description: A large dark hummingbird of forest edges, plantations, and gardens. Its black underparts, iridescent red cheeks, and red-purple tail are unique within its range.

name: White-gaped Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Northern australia (king sound, western australia to townsville, queensland)
description: A medium to large honeyeater with a sooty brown plumage and a bright pale patch between its eye and bill. Much larger than the similarly colored Dusky Honeyeater.

name: Costa Rican Brushfinch
rangeDescription: Highlands of southwestern costa rica and western panama (chiriquí)
description: Medium-sized sparrowlike bird with green back, gray eyebrow, black cheek, and white throat. Most similar to Black-striped Sparrow but with entire cheek black (not just eyeline); also compare with Chestnut-capped Brushfinch but note lack of rufous crown.
